text:
Philip Broberg left Saturday's 4-1 loss to Florida midway through the third period with a lower-body issue, which coach Jim Montgomery called precautionary, per NHL.com. He is day to day, and the Blues will notice: over the last ten games he has averaged more than 26 minutes a night, three more than before, topping out near 30 in a 1-0 win over Utah.

The offense is the new part. He has 13 points in 20 games, six on the power play, and he is on the ice for half of the Blues' power-play chances, up from 28% last season. His own chances have climbed from 0.24 to 0.41 expected goals per 60. He is also the fastest skater we track, 100th percentile in top speed by NHL Edge.

The catch is at five on five. St. Louis gets 44.6% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly eight points worse than without him, and his teammates have scored 8 more goals than expected while he plays, which props up his assists. Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among defensemen last season, so the talent isn't in doubt. The heavier load is. Watch how he looks when he's back.
headline: Broberg's minutes keep growing, and so do the questions
